newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian inflation eases, exports up - report.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian inflation eases, exports up - report.

text.p: Tanzania's annual rate of inflation eased to 18 percent during August -- from 18.2 per cent in July -- while the country registered a reduced trade deficit for the month, a Bank of Tanzania (BOT) report said.
In its monthly economic review for September, the BOT said the August inflation rate represented an improvement of 9.3 percentage points over the 27.3 percent recorded in August 1995.
The fall in inflation results from tight monetary and fiscal measures, while a satisfactory food supply situation also contributed to the decline, the report said.
However, the central bank cautioned that inflation may rise in September following a recent increase in fuel prices.
Tanzania's terms of trade in August saw a deficit of $66 million compared to $73.8 million for the same period last year.

Export earnings increased by 22 percent to $52.94 million during August compared to August 1995. Imports remained almost static, registering a small increase of 1.42 percent to $118.94 million compared to $117.28 for corresponding month in 1995.

Despite a decline in prices, Tanzania's traditional export mainstays, coffee, cotton and tea, brought higher earnings due to increased sales volume. These traditional exports, worth $29.92 million, were up by 25.1 per cent compared to August 1995. Export earnings from cashew nuts declined by 13.8 percent to $1.63 million compared to the same period last year.
The BOT forcast an improvement in coffee prices in the near future due to tight supply conditions and reduced global production.

In a move likely to be welcomed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the government's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has recommended the government "refrain from borrowing from the Bank of Tanzania" to further curb inflation, the report reveals.
Of the total amount of disbursed outstanding debt, ($6.5 billion) the government is the largest borrower accounting for 93.9 percent. Total private sector debt stood at 2.7 percent.

The BOT said the government's budgetary performance in August was encouraging with higher than expected collections in customs duty, sales tax, excise duty and non-tax revenue. On a monthly basis, collections for July and August were 36.2 billion shillings and 43.8 billion shillings respectively.
In August, the BOT purchased $26.3 million on the interbank foreign exchange market and paid off external debts worth $26.1 million. Tanzania's total debt at the end of August stood at $7.8 billion.

The shilling appreciated 0.6 percent in August with the exchange rate moving from 601.34 to the dollar in July to 597.6 in August -- due mainly to an increase in the supply of foreign exchange from pre-export earnings and a slackening in import demand.

On Tanzania's food security, the BOT said total food availability for 1996/1997 stood at 7.5 million tonnes against the recommended level of 7.1 million tonnes. However, the government's food security department is expected to purchase 90,000 tonnes of maize for the strategic grain reserve. (1$=590Tsh)
